title: Keep USB audio choices stable across PortAudio renumbering
problem: The control page saves PortAudio enumeration ids. When USB, Bluetooth, or display audio devices appear or disappear, those positions can point to a different microphone or speaker on the next start.
reproduce: At pinned revision 2540170, each device option value is its numeric id and formToSettings writes capture-id/playback-id while clearing the existing name pattern.
acceptance: Selecting capture or playback stores the device name pattern and clears the transient id; an existing id resolves to its current device and migrates on save; an unresolved saved name is visible; direct daemon id options remain supported.
repair: Use device names as picker values, resolve stored patterns and legacy ids against each new device list, save capture/playback patterns, and extend the served-page control gate and operator documentation.

verification.limitations: BCL proves the baseline writes transient ids and the candidate writes names, migrates legacy ids, exposes unresolved names, and embeds the checks in the live control-page arm. The upstream project built locally and all 524 hardware-free ctests passed. A station owner should still confirm the same interface is selected after a real USB re-enumeration.
verification.ownerCheck: Choose the radio USB interface on the Setup page and save. Stop the service, unplug an unrelated earlier-enumerated audio device, then restart and confirm /api/state stream.captureName (and sinkName when configured) still names the selected interface.

selection.reason: A fresh owner report demonstrates wrong-device capture and feedback after USB renumbering. The defect is deterministic in the pinned page, has no competing PR, and the project supplies a complete hardware-free control-page suite.

publish.commitMessage: fix(control-page): persist audio devices by name

negative.outputIncludes: device picker must carry the durable name
